column1: # Hand-written translation query answers, merged over the generated shader_facts.tsv by shader_split.py.
# Each row is  key <TAB> {"tex":{"<slot>":"<type>"}}  (types: 2d 2darray cube cubearray 3d buffer 1d 1darray 2dms 2dmsarray).
# Why these two: the translator defaults a texture handle's dimension to 2D when the answer table has no
# entry, and both programs then really sample a 3D texture. The host's own bind check reports it
# ("declares slot 0 as Metal type 2, texture ID is type 7 (NVN target 2 ...); bound as is"), and a 3D
# texture read through a texture2d is an undefined read, not a view Metal can make.
# STATUS 2026-11-07: these rows are NOT live. What is established:
#  - the row reaches the build: the "not in the answer table" note clears (10,848 -> 10,846);
#  - translation really re-runs with it: a fresh DMSH_CAS and just these two keys gives
#  - the type still does not change: the .metal declares texture2d, the note "texture handle A ...
#    using 2D" still fires 470 times, and d92d9b75e2cc7dad_b still mismatches at bind time.
# Slots 0, 1 and both together were tried. Program.cs reads _job["tex"][slot.ToString()] with the slot
# derived from the handle byte offset, so the remaining suspect is the job the translator receives.
# Next: add a job dump to dmsh_build (a source edit, so it bumps the chain) or capture the temp job file.
